Hi all —

I've reviewed Naomi's v3 redline and Sarah's notes. Summary of the legal positions and suggested next steps:

- Transfer mechanism: Redwood can accept the SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses) coupled with our EU DPA addendum. We cannot offer a blanket residency guarantee for all PII beyond the pilot scope without revising our hosting commitments; however, we will commit to EU-only hosting for the pilot as proposed.

- Subprocessors: our standard approach is notification + 30-day objection window for non-sensitive subprocessors; for subprocessors that process personal data (PII), FinEdge may request written approval. I've flagged two subprocessors in the CSV that handle tokenization and analytics which would fall into the "written approval" bucket.

- DocuSign: confirm that FinEdge requires DocuSign. We will prepare the DocuSign envelope and include an internal review step for signatories.

- Exception approvals: if procurement cannot meet the timeline, Redwood can issue a limited commercial exception (30 days) with the following controls: documented scope of pilot, EU-only processing for pilot, enhanced logging/audit retention for FinEdge, and a written attestation of no onward transfers beyond listed subprocessors. This exception must be signed off by Revenue (Marissa) and InfoSec (Rishi).
